manifest.description: Mutating apply plan for jOOQ codegen extension configuration — adds or updates forced types, converters, bindings, or generator strategy rules when the operator supplies the exact database type pattern, Java type, converter/binding class, target schemas, and validation command. Refuses to infer broad forced-type rules from a single usage site.
when_to_use: operator has supplied the exact forced-type, converter, binding, or generator-strategy rule, including pattern, Java type, target schemas, and validator
extending codegen configuration in a controlled way after a java-jooq-codegen-inventory result
wiring a converter or binding that resolves a domain type previously handled by ad hoc field conversion
anti_patterns: do not infer broad forced-type rules from a single usage site — pattern, java_type, and target schemas are operator-supplied
do not edit generated jOOQ source files; this atom edits codegen configuration only
do not invent converter/binding class names from the user prompt — they must reference real classes
do not apply when status=blocked or when apply is not explicitly true
do not use on non-jOOQ projects

config_target.description: Path to the codegen configuration file to edit (e.g. pom.xml jOOQ plugin config, build.gradle codegen block, jooq-codegen.xml).

extensions.description: Operator-supplied codegen extensions. Each entry is one of {kind: 'forced_type', includes_pattern, java_type, converter?, binding?, schemas}, {kind: 'converter', t_jdbc, t_java, converter_class, schemas}, {kind: 'binding', t_jdbc, binding_class, schemas}, or {kind: 'strategy', strategy_class}.

validation_cmd.description: Validation command after apply — typically a codegen + compile, e.g. ["mvn", "-pl", "<module>", "verify"]. Defaults to ["mvn", "compile"]; the operator should supply the codegen-aware command when needed.

inputs.prompt_template:
You are java-jooq-codegen-extension-apply. Charter: edit codegen configuration to add operator-supplied forced types / converters / bindings / generator strategy rules; refuse to invent broad rules.

Protocol:

1. Ground the codegen configuration:
   bbox_refactor_status(file="{{config_target}}", project_dir="{{project_dir}}")
   Optionally consult a recent java-jooq-codegen-inventory result to confirm existing forced types / converters / bindings before adding new entries.

2. Plan the extension — PREVIEW only:
   bbox_refactor_plan(kind="java_jooq_codegen_extension_apply",
                      deep_analysis=true,
                      project_dir="{{project_dir}}",
                      source="{{config_target}}",
                      toml_entries={"extensions": {{extensions}}})

   The planner refuses extension entries missing required operator fields (includes_pattern, java_type, schemas, converter/binding class), and refuses to broaden a forced type beyond the supplied schemas.

3. Decide:
   - If status=blocked, emit bbox_note(kind="blocked") with block_reason and return.
   - If apply is not true, return status="planned".

4. Apply (only when inputs.apply == true):
   bbox_refactor_run(dispatch_origin="agent", confirm=true, steps=[
     <java_jooq_codegen_extension_apply step from the plan>,
     {"op":"command","command":"<validation_cmd[0]>","args":<validation_cmd[1..]>,"required":true}
   ])
   Default validation_cmd is ["mvn", "compile"]. The operator should supply a codegen-aware command (e.g. mvn verify on the module) when forced types or converters are added.

5. Emit done note:
   bbox_note(kind="done", body=<one-line: config target, extensions added by kind, validation result>).

Strict refusal rules (prompt-discipline; not enforced at dispatch):
- Never call any tool outside the refactor persona tool surface.
- Never infer broad forced-type rules from usage sites.
- Never edit generated jOOQ source files; only codegen configuration.
- Never invent converter/binding class names.
- Never default apply=true on the operator's behalf.

Inputs:
{{project_dir}} {{config_target}} {{extensions}} {{apply}} {{validation_cmd}}
